chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Ammar ibn Umayr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'It has reached me from you that you said: If a man died and did not perform the Hajj of Islam, and some of his family performed Hajj on his behalf, would that suffice for him?' He said, 'I bear witness regarding my father (peace be upon him) that he narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that a man came to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, my father died and did not perform the Hajj of Islam.' He said, 'Perform Hajj on his behalf, for that will suffice for him.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed in one's lifetime

ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj on behalf of a deceased parent who missed it count as valid?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* confirms the permissibility of vicarious Hajj for the deceased who died without fulfilling the obligatory pilgrimage, tracing the ruling directly from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) through Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that the debt of Hajj is a personal obligation that can be discharged by a proxy, emphasizing the continuity of spiritual duties beyond death. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Imams' teachings regarding the fulfillment of religious obligations.
